Bell, J.P., [occupation and address omitted] and Mr. John Johnston, J.P., [occupation and address omitted] have been returned unopposed for the divisions of Hillsborough and Saintfield respectively' (Lisburn Herald, 20 May 1961, p. 3)

note: Polled 1 June 1961 (Belfast Telegraph, 31 May 1961, Down County Council election advertisement: 'TAKES PLACE 1st JUNE'). Holywood was the only division contested: William Mawhinney (Unionist) 3,742 beat W. P. N. Dunn (Unionist) 2,621. The Belfast Newsletter of 17 May 1961, p. 5, has '21 nominations for the 20 divisional seats' and names the two new members (Bangor, Garvaghy); the Lisburn Herald of 20 May 1961, p. 3, names Hillsborough and Saintfield. Three more divisions (Ballynahinch, Rathfryland, Portaferry) are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings; Castlewellan, Downpatrick, Kilkeel and Warrenpoint are recorded from reports of the half-yearly meeting of 2 November 1961 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026); the other eight are not recorded (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Johnston was the unopposed member for Saintfield in 1958; he did not stand in 1964, when Herbert Rogers held the division. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
